A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STReasoner work. Their main text and appendices are readable, and equations, figures, tables, prompts, and examples can be matched despite pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original ST-Bench experiments, CausalRivers evaluation, training ablations, sensitivity analyses, and five-run results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds model-scale comparisons, graph-removal checkpoint evaluations, and training-resource results.

M1.justification: The network-SDE synthesis pipeline, time-series encoder, three training stages, and S-GRPO reward and objective remain unchanged. The additional model-size experiments do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: ST-Align, the four ST-Bench tasks, synthetic domains and graph sizes, and CausalRivers coverage are unchanged. The new analyses reuse this coverage; graph-present and graph-absent inputs already occur in S-GRPO training in v1.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their comparison methods and training variants. New Table 4 extends Qwen3-based comparisons across model sizes rather than introducing a new comparison algorithm; its 8B control reproduces the existing Align+SFT results.

E3.justification: New Section 5.4 evaluates 4B and 14B models alongside 8B models. Table 5 adds Task 1 evaluations with and without graph input at RL steps 1, 11, 21, 31, 41, and 51. Existing dataset splits, task metrics, and Appendix D settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted analyses of model capacity and graph dependence across RL checkpoints. These supplement the retained training-stage and modality ablations, reward sensitivity analysis, extended-RL experiment, and case studies.

E5.justification: Appendix E retains the same five-run means and 95% confidence intervals, and Table 1 retains its p-value annotations. No additional uncertainty estimates, run counts, or statistical procedures are specified for the new analyses.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, real-world, ablation, and appendix results are unchanged. New Table 4 reports additional model-size results, including 96.69% Task 1 accuracy for STReasoner-14B. Table 5 reports a graph-input accuracy gap growing from 0.5 to 6.2 percentage points, and Table 6 adds energy and emissions results. These are supplementary results, not improvements to the retained same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The problem definition, network-SDE formulation, S-GRPO mathematics, and Appendix C reward definitions are unchanged. Adding equation number (2) to the policy objective is a presentation edit.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same ST-Bench, STReasoner, and S-GRPO claims, including the stated 17%–135% accuracy gains, 0.004× cost, and real-world generalization.

C2.justification: New Section 5.4 interprets the scaling results as evidence that the proposed method offers benefits beyond increasing model capacity. The checkpoint discussion reinforces the existing spatial-grounding interpretation. The stated limitations concerning real-world coverage and encoder expressiveness remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Table 6 discloses stage-specific runtime, GPU-hours, energy use, and emissions, including totals of 26.97 hours and 215.77 GPU-hours. Appendix D implementation settings, agent prompts, the code-access statement, and dataset license remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Citation lists expand to include works such as TimeMixer, TimeMixer++, and Time-MoE, and the epidemiology references change. Appendix A.4 adds an explicit distinction between graph-based spatio-temporal forecasting and multivariate forecasting. The central positioning against STReason and UrbanLLM remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a model-scale subsection, a checkpoint-analysis paragraph, and acknowledgments, and changes author order and corresponding-author annotations. Most existing prose and the appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables, relocates Figure 2 and the real-world comparison table, and swaps the numbering and placement of the sensitivity and spatial-reasoning figures. Appendix tables are renumbered. Existing graphical content is retained, with localized page reflow.

improvement.justification: The graph-removal analysis provides useful direct evidence that spatial input affects accuracy, while the scaling study and training-resource table broaden supporting evidence and transparency. The gain is limited: the scaling description is unclear about S-GRPO use across its rows, and the new analyses add no uncertainty estimates. The core method, primary results, and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged.
